Murrow, 1940 1:19 3 The War of the Worlds Orson Welles and the Mercury Theatre on the Air, 1938 1:30 On the other side: As it happened T / 1:20 · track 1 of 3 Oh, the humanity Herbert Morrison · 1937 · Lakehurst, New Jersey A Chicago radio reporter who came to record a routine airship landing instead describes the Hindenburg bursting into flames and falling, his voice breaking as he cries “oh, the humanity” until he can barely speak. Kennedy, 1963 1:13 On the other side: On the air T / 1:01 · track 1 of 3 Immediately Günter Schabowski · 1989 · East Berlin East Germany’s government spokesman reads out new rules letting people leave for the West through any border crossing, and when reporters ask when they start, he checks his notes and answers “sofort, unverzüglich”: immediately, without delay.
